properties.name: Peter
properties.death_claim: Circus of Nero / Vatican hill area (traditional martyrdom)
properties.burial: Tomb under high altar of St. Peter’s Basilica (Vatican Necropolis)
properties.structure: Papal Basilica of St. Peter (San Pietro in Vaticano)
properties.address: Piazza San Pietro, 00120 Città del Vaticano
properties.method: Crucifixion upside-down (head downward) at Rome under Nero — church tradition; Foxe follows this.
properties.last_statements: not attested in early sources as a fixed farewell speech; legendary Acts of Peter narrate request to be crucified head-down (late apocryphal).
properties.foxe: Foxe (IX. Peter): born Bethsaida; fisherman; 'supposed to have suffered martyrdom at Rome during the reign of the emperor Nero, being crucified with his head downward, at his own request.' Edition note: Foxe's Book of Martyrs (Project Gutenberg EBook #22400, compiled/abridged English edition; Ch. I History of Christian Martyrs to Nero). Editor footnote doubts whether Peter visited Rome.
properties.competing: Skull relics also claimed at Lateran; some Protestant editors (incl. Foxe ed. note) doubt Rome visit.
properties.notes: Strong continuous tradition from 2nd–4th c. memorial under Constantinian basilica. 20th-c. Scavi found a 2nd-c. trophy and bones contested as Peter’s. Tradition ≠ excavated name-tag proof.
properties.sources: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/22400/22400-h/22400-h.htm; https://www.basilicasanpietro.va/en/ (St Peter's Basilica official; Vatican Necropolis / Confessio); https://www.basilicasanpietro.va/en/san-pietro/the-necropolis (St Peter's Basilica official — Vatican Necropolis); https://gcatholic.org/churches/list/Apostles.htm
properties.method_sources: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/22400/22400-h/22400-h.htm (IX. Peter); Eusebius Ecclesiastical History 2.25 (citing Gaius/Dionysius on tropaia at Vatican); Tertullian Scorpiace 15; Origen via Eusebius 3.1
properties.last_statements_sources: Acts of Peter (apocryphal; 2nd c. tradition) — legendary; no Synoptic/Acts farewell text for Peter’s death
properties.biblical_or_early_refs: John 21:18–19 (Jesus foreshadows Peter’s death); Acts; Eusebius HE 2.25; 1 Clement 5

properties.name: Paul
properties.also_known_as: Saul of Tarsus; Apostle to the Gentiles
properties.death_claim: Along the Ostian Way (Aquae Salviae / Tre Fontane tradition for beheading)
properties.burial: Tomb under papal altar of St. Paul Outside the Walls
properties.structure: Papal Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls (San Paolo fuori le Mura)
properties.address: Piazzale San Paolo, 1, 00146 Roma RM, Italy
properties.method: Beheading by sword at Rome under Nero (citizen’s execution). Tertullian compares Paul’s beheading to John the Baptist’s (and Peter’s cross to Jesus’) as the apostolic pattern of matching their Lord’s mode of death by analogy of dignity.
properties.last_statements: 2 Timothy 4:6–8 commonly read as Paul’s farewell (‘I am already being poured out as a drink offering… I have finished the race’). No separate non-Christian transcript of scaffold words; later Acts of Paul have legendary speeches.
properties.foxe: Foxe (X. Paul): Jew of Benjamin, Tarsus; persecutions then prisoner at Rome; released; later Spain/France tradition; returning to Rome 'apprehended by order of Nero, and beheaded.' Also noted under Nero persecution with Peter. Foxe's Book of Martyrs (Project Gutenberg EBook #22400, compiled/abridged English edition; Ch. I History of Christian Martyrs to Nero).
properties.competing: Beheading locus often Tre Fontane abbey; burial basilica on Via Ostiense. Both traditional.
properties.notes: Sarcophagus under altar documented; inscription tradition PAULO APOSTOLO MART. Remains not forensically proven as Paul, but site continuity from Constantinian memoria is strong for a memorial tomb.
properties.sources: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/22400/22400-h/22400-h.htm; https://basilicasanpaolo.org/en/tomb/; https://www.vatican.va/various/basiliche/san_paolo/en/basilica/tomba.htm; https://www.vatican.va/various/basiliche/san_paolo/en/basilica/tomba.htm (Papal Basilica St Paul Outside-the-Walls tomb page)

properties.name: James the Just
properties.also_known_as: James the brother of Jesus; James of Jerusalem
properties.burial: Armenian Cathedral of St. James (Armenian Quarter) — traditional seat/tomb memory of James
properties.structure: Cathedral of St. James (Armenian Patriarchate of Jerusalem)
properties.address: Armenian Patriarchate Rd, Armenian Quarter, Old City, Jerusalem
properties.method: Thrown/pushed from Temple height, stoned, then struck with fuller’s club (Hegesippus); Josephus: stoned after Sanhedrin condemnation under high priest Ananus (~62 CE).
properties.last_statements: Hegesippus: prayed for his killers (‘Lord God, Father, forgive them…’) while being stoned — early but second-hand; honesty: may be stylized.
properties.foxe: Covered inside Foxe’s ‘James the Less’ entry (V): Jerusalem leadership; beaten/stoned; fuller’s club. Treated here as separate row because Josephus names James brother of Jesus, and Armenian Jerusalem tradition centers on him. Foxe's Book of Martyrs (Project Gutenberg EBook #22400, compiled/abridged English edition; Ch. I History of Christian Martyrs to Nero).
properties.competing: See also AP-09 Rome Santi Apostoli for ‘James Minor’ relics. Kidron ‘Tomb of St James’ is a separate monumental tomb misattribution.
properties.notes: Josephus gives non-Christian attestation of James’s death in Jerusalem. Cathedral marks living Armenian tradition; exact grave under church is tradition, not modern forensic proof.
properties.sources: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/22400/22400-h/22400-h.htm; https://gcatholic.org/churches/list/Apostles.htm (St James Cathedral / Armenian Quarter tradition; cf. Josephus Ant. 20.9.1); Josephus Ant. 20.9.1
properties.method_sources: Josephus Antiquities 20.9.1; Hegesippus via Eusebius HE 2.23; Foxe V (merged); Josephus Antiquities 20.9.1; Eusebius HE 2.23 (Hegesippus); https://gcatholic.org/churches/list/Apostles.htm
properties.biblical_or_early_refs: Gal 1:19; 2:9; Acts 15; 21:18; Josephus Ant. 20.9.1; Eusebius HE 2.23
